summary: Reproduced the original four-thread gfx950 device printf delay through piped stdout. torch.cuda.synchronize() completed before any stdout bytes were visible; fflush(NULL) and stdbuf -oL each exposed all four lines before teardown. Added the explicit flydsl.runtime.flush_device_printf() contract for use after synchronization, documented that it flushes host C stdio but does not synchronize GPU work, and added a timing-independent pipe regression that keeps the child alive until the parent observes thread IDs 0, 1, 2, and 3.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the change, stderr reported SYNCHRONIZED at 1.328389 s and EXITING at 4.328514 s, while the four stdout lines first became pipe-visible at 4.558322 s during teardown.
The explicit libc fflush control made all four lines visible at 1.025096 s, immediately after the synchronized/flush markers and about three seconds before EXITING.
The line-buffered control made all four lines visible at 1.022049 s, before SYNCHRONIZED was observed and about three seconds before EXITING.
The new FlyDSL helper made all four lines visible at 1.125482 s while the child remained alive until EXITING at 4.125532 s.

Timing-independent GPU pipe regression passed. The child synchronizes and flushes, then blocks on a control pipe; the parent verifies the live child and exactly four device lines with the independent CPU reference set {0,1,2,3} before releasing it.
Nine existing runtime unit tests passed.

A fresh compile emitted gpu.printf, LLVM calls to __ockl_printf_begin/__ockl_printf_append_string_n/__ockl_printf_append_args, and final ISA declaring amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx950 for hello_kernel_0.

remaining_limitations: The original hello(); torch.cuda.synchronize() sequence remains block-buffered when stdout is piped. The explicit API contract requires callers to invoke flydsl.runtime.flush_device_printf() after synchronizing the relevant stream or device.
flush_device_printf() calls fflush(NULL), so it flushes all host C stdio streams in the process, not only device printf output.
No C++ code changed, so the prepared native rebuild was not applicable; the loaded native extension remained /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir.
